payload.claim: Criterion 1's witness description, "It drives OLD_NAME_V2, NOOLD_NAME and old_name, in one file beside an uppercase hit, as text that reads nothing," is ambiguous about whether the genuine uppercase match sits in the same fixture file as the three near-miss strings or in a separate sibling file. If a cell builds the fixture with the true hit co-located in the same file as the near-misses, that file would be a valid reader under both a correct and a buggy (substring or case-insensitive) implementation alike, so that sub-test would fail to discriminate the two wrong versions it is paired with (the substring wrong version and the case-insensitive wrong version). A person should settle this reading before the cell starts.
